summary:
ALTR had its most proactive week on this account in months. Haleigh posted one message all week. Melissa confirmed the reel went live on all 23 repost accounts (10/9), sent the weekly leak recap on schedule (third week running), and posted an 'earnings and performance report for the last two weeks' (10/9). That is the first performance report in this chat in 2026, though it is a file and its contents are not visible in the export. On 10/11 Mayson answered her 10/4 IG link-safety question in writing, 7 days after she asked. Stephski sent the OF-withdrawal reminder on time (10/13) and the Oct 1-14 invoice on schedule (10/15). Two new team members, Jeremy Tarr (AM) and Spencer P (customs/uploads), introduced themselves the moment they were added on 10/13, the first group adds in five that were not silent.

The link answer is also the biggest new risk. Mayson re-issued the same domain, haleighsworld.vip, which restricted two of her IG accounts within 12 hours in June. He told her 'it won’t get flagged and it’s completely safe', and when she asked whether to use it on her main or her backup he answered 'Yes main is fine!'. Her main account was recently restored from a permanent disable. He gave the same assurance on 6/11, two days before the June restrictions. If her main gets restricted, that is the account-ending scenario she has been asking about since 11/2025.

Still open: Noah has been silent 18 days, and the $2.4k chargeback outcome he promised to report is 20 days overdue. The $1.7k fan's custom is unconfirmed, and customs ownership has changed hands again (Aroosha 10/3, now Spencer 10/13). Four wires (8/20, 9/7, 9/16, 10/6) are still unconfirmed, and the new invoice again points to banking 'at the bottom of the PDF'. The private live she agreed to on 9/14 is still unscheduled (33 days). Vivek's shadowban check is 79 days old.

Churn watch: 2 of 4 signals present, plus an engagement alarm. (1) Derrek has been silent 57 days (last message 8/20). (3) The phone-farm rollout promised 8/1 has no written proof after 76 days. Signal 2 is absent: both her questions got written answers, not call offers. Signal 4 is absent: 3 of 12 ALTR messages were billing. Her asks were 1 for the second week running, after 4 two weeks ago. This week's single ask was a follow-up to ALTR's own message, so she raised nothing new herself. She sent 1 message out of 13. A previously demanding client going quiet while service improves is the early shape of the exit pattern. If the Oct 1-14 invoice is paid unusually fast with no asks, treat that as a confirmed alarm.

health.rationale: 52, flat (53 on 10/9, 56 on 9/18). Better service and a quieter client offset each other. Up: her 10/4 IG question got a written answer (10/11, 7 days late), and she got a two-week earnings/performance report (10/9), the first in 2026 (file contents not visible). The 23-account reel repost went live, the leak recap is now weekly, the withdrawal reminder and invoice went out on time, and an AM (Jeremy Tarr) plus a customs/uploads owner (Spencer P) introduced themselves openly. Down: (1) Mayson put haleighsworld.vip back on her MAIN IG with a 'won’t get flagged' guarantee. That same domain restricted two of her accounts within 12 hours in June after the same assurance ('Yes It’s safe to put it in bio', 6/11). (2) Noah has been silent 18 days, with the $2.4k chargeback outcome 20 days overdue and the $1.7k fan's custom unconfirmed. (3) Four wires are still unconfirmed. (4) The private live is unscheduled at 33 days, and the shadowban check is at 79 days. (5) Churn signals 1 and 3 are present: Derrek silent 57 days, phone-farm promise 76 days with no proof. Signals 2 and 4 are absent. Client asks by week: ~2 (8/21), 0, 0, 0, 3 (9/18), 0 (9/25), 4 (10/2), 1 (10/9), 1 (10/16). Two consecutive weeks at 1 after a 4-ask week. This week's only ask was a follow-up to Mayson's message, and she sent 1 message in 13. Per the churn pattern, a demanding client going quiet is an alarm, not calm. Warm tone ('Amazing thank you!!!') and on-time payment history are not health signals on their own.
